added_failures_note: the reviewed run carries no baseline_suite/after_suite pair; derived from the two gate arms its manifest names -- gate-before-compat-fix.log (base rev c90682a28, 6 failed 54 passed EXIT=1) and gate4.log (head rev 512152937c714d1580f2c97689ab2a235a20bf81, 71 passed EXIT=0). The head arm reported zero FAILED/ERROR node ids, so the added set is empty and the count is a measured 0, not an unmeasured null.

findings.text: blocking: terminate routes a dead recorded pid that still carries a start tick into _signal_process_group, whose unguarded os.getpgid at reckon/crew/routing.py:3645 raises ProcessLookupError; reproduced end-to-end, a dead supervisor pid plus its recorded tick raises ProcessLookupError while the same run with pid_start_time None ends the reparented worker, so `crew stop` on a run whose supervisor already exited and any repeat stop crash instead of reaping the worker.

follow-on: the reparented-worker stop test writes pid_start_time None, a shape a real run pointer never has because reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2053 records pid and pid_start_time together, so the test takes the else branch and passes while the real record shape crashes.

follow-on: `if not expected_start_time` treats an absent recorded tick as a refusal to signal, the opposite stance to _root_names_the_recorded_process at reckon/crew/routing.py:3421 in the same commit, so terminate can select a live pid with no recorded tick and get a refusal instead of a stop.
follow-on: the after-arm log's command line carries angle-bracket placeholders rather than the literal command, so the head revision's gate cannot be re-run from the log alone.
